title: Separate CUDA output allocation from the timed resident GEMM kernel
finding: The CUDA value labelled resident kernel time still created a fresh GEMM output tensor on every warmup and measured repetition through torch.matmul. Output allocation/allocator behavior therefore remained entangled with the repeated compute boundary, while the one-shot decomposition exposed no allocation term. That made the CUDA resident-kernel comparison less strict than the corrected packed-CPU timing boundary from G1-EXP-TENSOR-GPU-04.
change: allocate the padded CUDA output tensor exactly once after both dense inputs are resident
record output_allocate_ms separately from sparse-to-dense packing, GEMM kernel timing, and readback/canonicalization
execute every warmup and timed 2-D GEMM through torch.mm(..., out=product) so the caller-owned output buffer is reused
include output allocation in one_shot_end_to_end_ms but exclude it from cpu_over_resident_gpu_kernel
retain the existing VRAM admission estimate, which already accounts for one resident GEMM output matrix
add a CPU-only fake-torch regression proving the resident helper forwards the exact caller-owned output buffer
mechanically refuse regrowth of torch.matmul allocation inside the probe's repeated resident path

timing_contract.pack_to_device_ms: build the two dense CUDA input matrices from canonical CSR support
timing_contract.output_allocate_ms: allocate the reusable padded GEMM output tensor once
timing_contract.kernel_ms: CUDA-event time for torch.mm with an already allocated out= buffer; no output allocation in the repeated resident path
timing_contract.readback_and_canonicalize_ms: threshold Boolean support, copy it to CPU and rebuild the canonical TypedRelationBlock
timing_contract.resident_kernel_ratio: CPU CSR oracle divided by median preallocated CUDA kernel only
timing_contract.one_shot_ratio: CPU CSR oracle divided by the complete one-shot decomposition above
